results.title: Brain region identification
results.question: What are the major subdivisions of the Drosophila mushroom body?
results.response:
The major subdivisions of the Drosophila [mushroom body](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00005801 "Open mushroom body in Virtual Fly Brain") are the calyx, pedunculus, and mushroom body lobe system. This information comes from the VFB database. VFB records show that the mushroom body is divided into these three parts: the calyx, which receives sensory interneuron afferents; the pedunculus, a thick axon bundle extending from the calyx to the base of the lobes; and the mushroom body lobe system, which consists of a vertical branch and a medial branch. 

VFB holds a range of data related to the mushroom body, including images, neurons with some part in the mushroom body, and parts of the mushroom body. Specifically, VFB has annotated [602](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005801,NeuronsPartHere "Run in VFB: Neurons with some part in mushroom body") neurons with some part in the mushroom body, [601](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005801,NeuronsSynaptic "Run in VFB: Neurons with synaptic terminals in mushroom body") neurons with synaptic terminals in the mushroom body, and [176](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005801,PartsOf "Run in VFB: Parts of mushroom body") parts of the mushroom body. 

For further information, you can explore the available data in VFB, such as the images of the mushroom body, the neurons with synaptic terminals in the mushroom body, or the parts of the mushroom body.

results.title: Neuron type classification
results.question: What types of Kenyon cells exist in the adult Drosophila brain?
results.response: The adult Drosophila brain contains several types of Kenyon cells. According to VFB, subclasses of [Kenyon cell](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00003686 "Open Kenyon cell in Virtual Fly Brain") include [37](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00003686,SubclassesOf "Run in VFB: Subclasses of Kenyon cell") types, such as [[KCab-c](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00110929 "Open KCab-c in Virtual Fly Brain")(i)](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00049111 "Open KCab-c(i) in Virtual Fly Brain"), KCab-c, [KCg-m](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00111061 "Open KCg-m in Virtual Fly Brain"), [Kenyon cell of main calyx](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00047926 "Open Kenyon cell of main calyx in Virtual Fly Brain"), and [gamma Kenyon cell](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00100247 "Open gamma Kenyon cell in Virtual Fly Brain"). VFB also records that there are alpha/beta, alpha'/beta', and gamma Kenyon cells, which are further subdivided into subtypes. VFB holds 37 records of subclasses of Kenyon cell and provides various data related to Kenyon cells, including images, scRNAseq data, transgene expression, and connectivity classes. For more specific information, you can explore the available data, such as listing all available images of Kenyon cell, which totals [32328](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00003686,ListAllAvailableImages "Run in VFB: List all available images of Kenyon cell") records, or examining the downstream and upstream connectivity classes for Kenyon cell, which comprise [10073](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00003686,DownstreamClassConnectivity "Run in VFB: Downstream connectivity classes for Kenyon cell") and [11243](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00003686,UpstreamClassConnectivity "Run in VFB: Upstream connectivity classes for Kenyon cell") records, respectively.

results.title: Central complex structure
results.question: What are the main components of the Drosophila central complex and what functions are they associated with?
results.response:
To address the question about the main components of the Drosophila central complex and their associated functions, we need to look at available data and literature. 

The Drosophila central complex is a crucial structure in the insect brain, involved in various functions including spatial memory, navigation, and the control of locomotor behaviors. The main components of the central complex include the ellipsoid body, the protocerebral bridge, the noduli, and the fan-shaped body.

The ellipsoid body is thought to be involved in spatial memory and orientation (as discussed in  Seelig and Jayaraman, 2013, PMID: 23332763, and  Wolff et al., 2015, PMID: 26457613). The protocerebral bridge is associated with the processing of visual information for navigation (discussed in  Wolff et al., 2015, PMID: 26457613). The fan-shaped body has been implicated in the control of locomotor behaviors and spatial memory (discussed in  Pfeiffer and Homberg, 2014, PMID: 25280975, and  Heinze and Homberg, 2007, PMID: 17920017). The noduli are also part of this complex but less is known about their specific functions compared to the other components.

VFB does not currently hold detailed, specific data on the functions of each component of the Drosophila central complex. For more detailed information, consulting specific publications or databases focused on Drosophila neuroscience would be necessary.

results.title: Circuit motif
results.question: Describe the dopaminergic input to mushroom body output neurons (MBONs). Which DAN types connect to which MBON types?
results.response:
The dopaminergic input to mushroom body output neurons (MBONs) is provided by adult dopaminergic mushroom body input neurons. VFB holds various data related to these neurons, including their subclasses, scRNAseq data, transgene expression, and upstream and downstream connectivity classes. For example, VFB has annotated [69](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00047953,SubclassesOf "Run in VFB: Subclasses of MBON") subclasses of MBON and [158](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00047953,TransgeneExpressionHere "Run in VFB: Transgene expression in MBON") records of transgene expression in MBON. 

To determine which specific types of adult dopaminergic mushroom body input neurons (also known as Dopaminergic Neurons, DANs) connect to which types of MBONs, one can query the upstream connectivity classes for MBON, of which VFB has annotated [23753](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00047953,UpstreamClassConnectivity "Run in VFB: Upstream connectivity classes for MBON") records. Similarly, querying the downstream connectivity classes for [adult dopaminergic mushroom body input neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00049839 "Open adult dopaminergic mushroom body input neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"), which are available in VFB, may provide insight into the specific connections between DAN types and MBON types. 

VFB does not currently hold specific information on the connectivity between [larval mushroom body dopaminergic neuron h1](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00111634 "Open larval mushroom body dopaminergic neuron h1 in Virtual Fly Brain") and MBONs in the adult stage, but it does have data on the transgene expression and connectivity classes for larval mushroom body dopaminergic neuron h1. 

To further investigate the connections between specific DAN types and MBON types, one could run queries on the upstream and downstream connectivity classes for these neurons using VFB.

results.title: Neuron characterisation
results.question: What is known about the LPLC2 visual neuron type? Where is it, what does it connect to, and what is its function?
results.response: The LPLC2 visual neuron type is known to be a lobula plate-lobula columnar neuron. VFB records show that it has a distinct dendritic arbor in each lobula plate layer, extending outwards from the main fiber in the direction of motion detection for the layer. According to the VFB summary of neuron profile, its cell body lies in the dorsal area of the lateral cell body rind, as described by Wu et al., 2016. The connectome data indicates that it is located in the lobula plate, with dendritic arbors in each layer. VFB does not currently hold detailed data on its specific connections to other neurons. The function of the LPLC2 visual neuron type is related to motion detection, as its dendritic arbors extend in the direction of motion detection for each layer, as described by Klapoetke et al., 2017.

results.title: Complete neuron profile
results.question: Give me a comprehensive profile of the giant fiber neuron: its anatomy, connectivity, available driver lines, and relevant publications.
results.response:
The [giant fiber neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00004020 "Open giant fiber neuron in Virtual Fly Brain") is a large adult descending neuron that controls jump escape behavior, with a unique anatomy and connectivity profile. It has a large cell body located posterior to the lower protocerebrum and a large descending axon that is several times larger than any other axon in the cervical connective. The axon enters the cervical connective via the posterior cerebro-cervical fascicle and descends on the ipsilateral side in the dorsal cervical fasciculus. In the brain, the giant fiber neuron has dendritic arborization in the ipsilateral zones A and B of the antennal mechanosensory and motor center, where it receives substantial input from zone A and B Johnston organ neurons. It also arborizes in the posterior ventrolateral protocerebrum and gorget. The giant fiber neuron forms electrical synapses with downstream motor and premotor neurons at the inframedial bridge and at the axonal lateral bend.

VFB holds various data related to the giant fiber neuron, including [23](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004020,ListAllAvailableImages "Run in VFB: List all available images of DNp01") images of DNp01, [5](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004020,SplitsTargeting "Run in VFB: Splits targeting DNp01") splits targeting DNp01, and [14](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004020,TransgeneExpressionHere "Run in VFB: Transgene expression in DNp01") records of transgene expression in DNp01. Additionally, VFB has annotated [389](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004020,DownstreamClassConnectivity "Run in VFB: Downstream connectivity classes for DNp01") downstream connectivity classes and [472](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004020,UpstreamClassConnectivity "Run in VFB: Upstream connectivity classes for DNp01") upstream connectivity classes for DNp01.

Available driver lines for the giant fiber neuron include [P{R48A11-GAL4.DBD} ∩ P{R30C01-p65.AD} expression pattern](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/VFBexp_FBtp0121835FBtp0118557 "Open P{R48A11-GAL4.DBD} ∩ P{R30C01-p65.AD} expression pattern in Virtual Fly Brain"), [P{R68A06-GAL4.DBD} ∩ P{R25C08-p65.AD} expression pattern](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/VFBexp_FBtp0116198FBtp0118471 "Open P{R68A06-GAL4.DBD} ∩ P{R25C08-p65.AD} expression pattern in Virtual Fly Brain"), [P{R79H02-GAL4.DBD} ∩ P{R14A01-p65.AD} expression pattern](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/VFBexp_FBtp0122311FBtp0118233 "Open P{R79H02-GAL4.DBD} ∩ P{R14A01-p65.AD} expression pattern in Virtual Fly Brain"), [P{R79H02-GAL4.DBD} ∩ P{R25C08-p65.AD} expression pattern](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/VFBexp_FBtp0122311FBtp0118471 "Open P{R79H02-GAL4.DBD} ∩ P{R25C08-p65.AD} expression pattern in Virtual Fly Brain"), and [P{VT004455-GAL4.DBD} ∩ P{R10A12-p65.AD} expression pattern](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/VFBexp_FBtp0122730FBtp0118153 "Open P{VT004455-GAL4.DBD} ∩ P{R10A12-p65.AD} expression pattern in Virtual Fly Brain").

Relevant publications for the giant fiber neuron include Thomas and Wyman (1984), Koto et al. (1981), Power (1948), Ito et al. (2014), Kamikouchi et al. (2009), Kennedy and Broadie (2018), and Allen et al. (1998).

results.response: NBLAST is a method to quantify morphological similarity, as described in the documentation.
